candidate.content: Aluminum acts as a sacrificial element, reducing the Cr dissolution rate by forming a redox couple (Al/AlCl3) that thermodynamically disfavors the dissolution of Co, Ni, and Fe.
candidate.evidence_span: This suggests that Al in the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 acted as a sacrificial element and reduced Cr dissolution rate in the molten salt compared to DS2205. Redox control technique has been utilized for corrosion mitigation in molten fluoride and chloride salts. Dissolution of Al and Cr into the molten salt resulted in the formation of AlCl3 and CrCl2, which formed a redox couple of Al/AlCl3 and Cr/CrCl2. At the redox potential, Co, Ni, and Fe become relatively nobler and their dissolution is thermodynamically unfavorable.
